answer:
The feature is **iterative index scans**, added in pgvector 0.8.0. "Starting with 0.8.0, you can enable iterative index scans, which will automatically scan more of the index until enough results are found (or it reaches `hnsw.max_scan_tuples` or `ivfflat.max_probes`)." [pgvector/README.md]

The cause is that "queries with filtering can return less results since filtering is applied *after* the index is scanned." [pgvector/README.md]

To enable it for HNSW, the README gives "SET hnsw.iterative_scan = strict_order;" for exact distance ordering, or "SET hnsw.iterative_scan = relaxed_order;" for better recall with slightly out-of-order results. For IVFFlat, it gives "SET ivfflat.iterative_scan = relaxed_order;". [pgvector/README.md]
